To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Fourier analysis can be used to predict the performance of numerical methods in the context of LES.
the DG method is a good choice in LES because it can be made arbitrarily dispersive and dissipative.

(1) the DG method has a better dispersion/dissipation balance in the entire wavenumbers, and that the RKDG scheme has a better dispersion balance than the DG scheme in the entire wavy numbers; (2) for a given time step, the CD and FD methods are more dissipative than the DG scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Fourier analysis of the DG, FD and CD methods in both space and in time.
the Fourier analysis of several numerical methods in the context of large eddy simulation, and the comparison of these methods in dispersion and dissipative properties.
the Fourier analysis of DG, RKDG, and FD methods for conservation laws, and their applications to LES.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DG scheme has the best overall performance in dispersion/dissipation properties among the methods under consideration.
the DG, CD and central FD schemes have comparable dispersion and dissipation behaviors in the low wavy-number regime.
DG and RKDG have a superior dispersion/dissipation properties over FD and CD methods in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DG schemes are the best choice among the methods considered here, in terms of the overall dissipation, for LES of vortex-dominated turbulent flows, especially in the low waved number range.
the DG scheme is more accurate than the CD scheme, but less accurate than the central FD scheme in terms of the overall dissipation in the entire wavenumbers range.
the DG method is a promising candidate for large eddy simulation (or direct numerical simulation) of turbulent flows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DG and CD methods are more dissipative than central FD methods in the wavenumber range where the physical-mode is a good approximation.
DG schemes are not always more dissipative than FD and CD schemes.
the numerical dissipation of DG schemes can be controlled by the choice of numerical flux and the time integration scheme.
